UED_May2025 · GPT platform check
10 fC · 1.6-cell gun · −68 MV/m, 37° · 62.5k macroparticles · 3.1 MeV

Linux GPT reproduces the Windows run

Same deck (UED_beamline.in), same analysis notebook, two builds of GPT. The Linux run on S3DF matches the Windows reference in energy, emittance, spot size and transmission. Bunch length and energy spread come out slightly lower.

Windows · reference

GPT on Windows, gpt -j 16. Numbers and figures as saved in check_single_run_1p6cell_10fC.ipynb.

Linux · S3DF

GPT 3.43 Linux build (CentOS 7, AVX2) on sdfiana016, gpt -j 16, 2 min 26 s. The same notebook re-run on the new output.

  • matchKinetic energy is identical to the reference's printed precision. Transmitted charge and emittance agree within the Linux run-to-run scatter.
  • at edgeBeam size is 0.3% larger on Linux, right at the edge of the scatter.
  • outsideBunch length is 1–2% lower and energy spread 3–5% lower on Linux, in every run.

Notebook figures

Both columns come from the same notebook code. Switch a figure to Windows or Linux to flip between them in place.

Beam along the line

Bunch length, emittance and rms size against z. Dashed line: sample plane.

The curves overlap everywhere except the step where the collimator cuts the beam: 0.68 m on Windows, 0.60 m on Linux. See the first note below.

Energy and energy spread

Mean kinetic energy and relative energy spread against z.

The gun takes the beam to 3.1 MeV within the first 0.1 m on both. Downstream, the Linux energy spread sits a little lower.

Phase space at the sample plane

Longitudinal, transverse and spot plots at z = 1.557 m.

Same energy chirp (γ from 7.0641 to 7.0610 across ±30 fs), same phase-space tilt, same ±60 µm spot.

Reading the comparison

The collimator step moves

GPT removes the clipped particles at the end of an integration step, but screens are interpolated inside the step. Screens between the iris (0.5575 m) and the end of that step still record all 62.5k particles. Windows took a longer step there, so its drop shows at 0.68 m against 0.59–0.63 m on Linux. Screens past about 0.7 m are unaffected.

Linux runs scatter by about 1%

With several threads, space charge is summed in a different order on each run. The 47 µm-radius collimator turns those tiny differences into a different set of surviving particles, so transmission varies by about 1% between runs. Single-thread runs repeat bit for bit.

Bunch length and energy spread

These two are the only quantities outside the Linux scatter, in the same direction in every run. The notebook doesn't record which GPT version made the reference, so a version or step-size difference on Windows is the most likely cause.
